title: GitHub - palamim/usagent: macOS menu bar app showing Claude subscription usage (5-hour + weekly limits) at a glance
excerpt: macOS menu bar app showing Claude subscription usage (5-hour + weekly limits) at a glance - palamim/usagent
content_html:
Tracks Claude's two usage clocks — the 5-hour rolling window and the weekly cap — and shows whichever is closer to its limit in the menu bar. Click it for both: percent used and time to reset, side by side.

Reads your Claude Code OAuth token from the macOS Keychain — the same system credential store the OS itself uses, not a plaintext file. Reading it triggers a macOS authorization prompt for your login password, and you can revoke access at any time in Keychain Access.app. Makes no network calls except to Anthropic's own endpoint. The source is short enough to read yourself before trusting it with your credentials.

Unofficial and not affiliated with Anthropic — built by reverse-engineering an undocumented endpoint (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage), so it may break without warning if that changes.

No dock icon, no settings, no telemetry.

Install

Pick one — both end up with usagent.app on disk.

Option A: Download

  1. Grab the latest usagent-X.Y.Z.zip from Releases.
  2. Unzip it and move usagent.app to /Applications.
  3. Right-click usagent.app → Open (don't double-click) the first time. macOS will warn it's from an unidentified developer — that's because the app is ad-hoc signed, not notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID. Click Open anyway. This warning only appears once; after that it launches normally, including via Login Items.

After the first manual install, ./Scripts/update.sh (or make update) automates picking up new releases — see Update below.

Option B: Build from source

Requires the Xcode command line tools (Swift 5.9+, macOS 13+).

git clone https://github.com/palamim/usagent.git
cd usagent
make app     # builds usagent.app with a proper Info.plist (no dock icon)
make open    # builds and opens it

A locally built app isn't quarantined by Gatekeeper (that only happens to files downloaded through a browser), so no right-click-to-open step is needed here. Move usagent.app to /Applications if you want it to live somewhere permanent.

make run (plain swift run) also works for quick iteration while developing — it flashes a dock icon briefly on launch since it isn't run from a bundle, which is expected and harmless.

Tests

swift test runs the UsageStore unit tests (state-machine behavior, binding-clock selection) against a mocked UsageFetching, no network or Keychain access needed. Requires full Xcode.app, not just the Command Line Tools — that's an XCTest requirement on macOS, not something this project controls. CI (.github/workflows/tests.yml) runs the suite on every push, since GitHub's macOS runners ship with Xcode preinstalled.

Run at login

Once usagent.app is somewhere permanent (e.g. /Applications), add it to Login Items:

System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Open at Login → + → select usagent.app.

If you rebuild from source, make app overwrites the same path, so you won't need to re-add it as a login item afterward.

Update

make update    # or ./Scripts/update.sh

Downloads the latest GitHub release, quits any running usagent, replaces /Applications/usagent.app with the new build, clears the Gatekeeper quarantine flag so it opens without a right-click, then reopens it. Prompts to add it to Login Items if it isn't already there. Requires the gh CLI, authenticated (gh auth login).

First launch: Keychain prompt

The OAuth token lives in the macOS Keychain under the service name Claude Code-credentials, created by the Claude Code CLI — not by this app. The first time usagent reads it, macOS will prompt for your login password to authorize access. Click "Always Allow" (not "Allow") — otherwise you'll be prompted again on every launch or every refresh.

If you're prompted repeatedly even after that, the Keychain item's ACL may have been reset (e.g. after rebuilding with a different code signature). Re-authorizing once with "Always Allow" fixes it again.

Why direct API calls, not a companion state file

Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor invites native menu bar apps to consume its --write-state output instead of calling Anthropic's endpoint directly. We call the endpoint directly instead: its own "official" data source for that state file is the same OAuth usage endpoint (behind an opt-in --api flag), so routing through it would mean running a separate Python tool as a background process for no benefit — just a dependency and a moving part this app doesn't need.

Worth naming the other prior art too: ccusage is the terminal tool most people reach for first, and does that well. usagent isn't trying to replace it — it covers the case a terminal or status-line tool doesn't: a persistent, at-a-glance menu bar indicator you're not running as a command.

Plan support

  • Pro: what this app is built and tested against. five_hour and seven_day are the two clocks shown; everything else in the response is null and ignored.
  • Max: should work unchanged for the two main clocks — same shape, higher limits. Max plans are also expected to populate seven_day_opus, a separate (tighter) weekly sub-cap on Opus, which usagent shows as an extra "Weekly Opus" row and folds into the "closest to limit" calculation when present. This is implemented defensively but not verified against a real Max account — if the field's shape or meaning turns out to be different, please open an issue with a redacted response body.
  • Free: out of scope. Free-tier accounts don't get Claude Code CLI access, so there's no OAuth token for this app to read in the first place.
  • Team / Enterprise: unhandled. These likely use org-pooled limits rather than the personal five-hour/weekly windows this app is built around — probably a different feature, not a tweak.

Notes

  • The endpoint (https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage) is undocumented. It could change or disappear without notice.
  • Refreshes on a 60s timer and on click, throttled to at most once per 15s to avoid hammering the endpoint.

content_html_zh:
跟踪 Claude 的两个使用时钟 - 5 小时滚动窗口和每周上限 - 并在菜单栏中显示最接近其限制的那个。 单击它可同时查看：已使用百分比和重置时间。

从 macOS 钥匙串读取您的 Claude Code OAuth 令牌 - 操作系统本身使用的相同系统凭证存储，而不是纯文本文件。 读取它会触发 macOS 授权提示，提示您输入登录密码，您可以随时在 Keychain Access.app 中撤销访问权限。 除 Anthropic 自己的端点外，不进行任何网络调用。 来源足够短，您可以自行阅读，然后再信任它。

非官方且不隶属于 Anthropic — 通过对未记录的端点进行逆向工程构建 (api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage)，因此如果发生变化，它可能会在没有警告的情况下崩溃。

没有停靠图标，没有设置，没有遥测。

安装

选择一个 — 两者最终都会在磁盘上生成 usnt.app。

选项 A：下载

  1. 从发行版中获取最新的usagent-X.Y.Z.zip。
  2. 解压缩并将 ususnt.app 移至 /Applications。
  3. 右键单击 usnt.app → 第一次打开（不要双击）。 macOS 会警告它来自身份不明的开发者 - 这是因为该应用程序是临时签名的，没有使用付费的 Apple 开发者 ID 进行公证。 仍然单击“打开”。 该警告仅出现一次；之后它会正常启动，包括通过登录项启动。

第一次手动安装后，./Scripts/update.sh（或 make update）会自动获取新版本 - 请参阅下面的更新。

选项 B：从源代码构建

需要 Xcode 命令行工具（Swift 5.9+、macOS 13+）。

git clone https://github.com/palamim/usagent.git
cd usagent
make app     # builds usagent.app with a proper Info.plist (no dock icon)
make open    # builds and opens it

本地构建的应用程序不会被 Gatekeeper 隔离（这种情况仅发生在通过浏览器下载的文件上），因此此处不需要右键单击打开步骤。 如果您希望 usnt.app 永久驻留在某处，请将其移至 /Applications。

make run (plain swift run) 也适用于开发时的快速迭代 - 它在启动时会短暂闪烁一个停靠图标，因为它不是从捆绑包中运行，这是预期的且无害的。

Tests

swift test 针对模拟的UsageFetching 运行UsageStore 单元测试（状态机行为、绑定时钟选择），无需网络或钥匙串访问。 需要完整的 Xcode.app，而不仅仅是命令行工具——这是 macOS 上的 XCTest 要求，而不是该项目控制的东西。 CI (.github/workflows/tests.yml) 在每次推送时都会运行该套件，因为 GitHub 的 macOS 运行程序预装了 Xcode。

登录时运行

一旦 usnt.app 永久存在（例如 /Applications），请将其添加到登录项：

系统设置 → 常规 → 登录项和扩展 → 登录时打开 → + → 选择 usnt.app。

如果您从源代码重建，则 make app 会覆盖相同的路径，因此您之后无需将其重新添加为登录项。

更新

make update    # or ./Scripts/update.sh

下载最新的 GitHub 版本，退出任何正在运行的 usnt，用新版本替换 /Applications/usagent.app，清除 Gatekeeper 隔离标志，以便无需右键单击即可打开，然后重新打开它。 如果登录项尚不存在，则提示将其添加到其中。 需要 gh CLI，经过身份验证（gh auth 登录）。

首次启动：钥匙串提示

OAuth 令牌位于 macOS 钥匙串中，服务名称为 Claude Code-credentials，由 Claude Code CLI 创建，而不是由此应用程序创建。 当用户第一次读取它时，macOS 将提示您输入登录密码以授权访问。 单击“始终允许”（而不是“允许”），否则每次启动或每次刷新时都会再次提示您。

如果在此之后仍反复提示您，则钥匙串项目的 ACL 可能已被重置（例如，使用不同的代码签名重建后）。 使用“始终允许”重新授权一次即可修复此问题。

为什么直接 API 调用，而不是配套的状态文件

Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor 邀请本机菜单栏应用程序使用其 --write-state 输出，而不是直接调用 Anthropic 的端点。 我们直接调用端点：该状态文件自己的“官方”数据源是相同的 OAuth 使用端点（在 opt-in --api 标志后面），因此通过它进行路由意味着运行一个单独的 Python 工具作为后台进程，没有任何好处 - 只是这个应用程序不需要的依赖项和移动部分。

其他现有技术也值得一提：ccusage 是大多数人首先使用的终端工具，并且做得很好。 ususnt 并不试图取代它——它涵盖了终端或状态行工具所不具备的情况：一个持久的、一目了然的菜单栏指示器，您不作为命令运行。

计划支持

  • 优点：这个应用程序是根据什么构建和测试的。 Five_hour 和 Seven_day 是显示的两个时钟；响应中的其他所有内容均为空并被忽略。
  • Max：两个主时钟应该保持不变——形状相同，限制更高。 预计最大计划还将填充 Seven_day_opus，这是 Opus 上一个单独的（更严格的）每周子上限，它的用法显示为额外的“每周 Opus”行，并在存在时折叠到“最接近限制”计算中。 这是防御性实现的，但未针对真实的 Max 帐户进行验证 - 如果字段的形状或含义不同，请使用经过编辑的响应正文打开问题。
  • 免费：超出范围。 免费层帐户无法获得 Claude Code CLI 访问权限，因此该应用程序首先没有可供读取的 OAuth 令牌。
  • 团队/企业：未处理。 这些可能使用组织池限制，而不是该应用程序构建的个人五小时/每周窗口 - 可能是不同的功能，而不是调整。

Notes

  • 端点（https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage）未记录。 它可能会更改或消失，恕不另行通知。
  • 在 60 秒计时器和点击时刷新，限制为最多每 15 秒一次，以避免对端点造成影响。
